what: The Indian Mahāyoga and Anuyoga tantras, the Kagye heruka cycles and their empowerments, brought by Padmasambhava, Vimalamitra and others and translated in the 8th-9th c.

evidence.detail: Nyingma histories of the kama lineage
Colophons naming Indian translators (Kunjed Gyalpo, Dupa Do; local Derge)

what: A sudden, non-conceptual approach to awakening; shared vocabulary of non-meditation

evidence.detail: Critics (Sakya Paṇḍita) allege derivation; the Nyingma deny it, distinguishing Atiyoga from Chan (Samten Migdrön)
Chan and early rdzogs chen texts were copied side by side at Dunhuang; influence debated

what: Shared Great Perfection terminology (kun gzhi, rig pa, khregs chod, thod rgal, rainbow body), the nine-vehicle structure, treasure revelation and tantric cycles

evidence.detail: Parallel Dzogchen and treasure vocabulary in both canons
Each tradition claims priority; some revealers (Dorje Lingpa) revealed both Buddhist and Bön treasures

what: Heart-essence (snying thig) instruction and the union of Mahāmudrā and Dzogchen

evidence.detail: The Third Karmapa's Nyingthig lineage; Karma Chagme's union of Mahāmudrā and Dzogchen

what: Treasure cycles and Dzogchen as the shared core of the non-sectarian movement (Rinchen Terdzö)
Buddha-nature doctrine read as the ground of the Great Perfection (Mipham's luminosity-emptiness)
